title: I sleep badly, so I started recording myself. On the tape I sit up at 4 AM and say goodbye.
story:
My doctor suggested I film myself sleeping, to see if I was sleepwalking. I set my phone on the dresser and pressed record.

In the morning I watched it at triple speed. Nothing for hours. Then at 4:03 AM, I sat straight up in bed, eyes open, and turned toward the closed bedroom door.

I played that part slowly.

On the tape, I said, "Okay. I'm ready."

My voice sounded polite, even a little tired. Then I got up and walked to the door and stood very close to it, as if listening.

I deleted the video. Next night I tried again, because I needed to know.

Same time. This time I whispered, "Tell her I said goodbye."

I don't have anyone to say goodbye to.

On the third night, I did something different. I stayed awake in the dark, watching the clock, with the phone recording on the dresser. At 4:03 my body stayed completely still, but something in the room moved.

I watched the footage later. I watched myself lying awake, rigid, eyes wide. And standing beside the bed, in perfect focus, I saw myself.

Standing over me, smiling, with its hand on the doorknob.

"Thank you," it said.

My turn now.
premise: sleep recording shows me answering someone; the recorded me says the lines the thing needs
